ui_bugs.issue: useEffect runs `if (!user) navigate('/login?next=...')` on first render while user is still `undefined` (auth fetchMe pending). For an already-logged-in user clicking 'Upgrade to Creator →' from /pricing, the page mounts, the redirect fires before /auth/me resolves, the user is bounced to /login, and the `next` param is double-encoded into itself producing a recursive `/login?next=%2Flogin%3Fnext%3D...` URL. Net effect: the entire /plan-checkout page is unreachable for logged-in users. A React error-boundary console.warn was also observed (component crash inside PlanCheckout). Fix: gate redirect on `user === null` (not `!user`), AND show a Loader while `user === undefined`.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL) PlanCheckout.jsx line 28: change `if (!user)` to `if (user === null)` and render a Loader while `user === undefined`. Without this fix the entire /plan-checkout page is unreachable for logged-in users (Pricing → CTA → infinite /login?next= recursion).

Investigate the React error boundary warning thrown inside <PlanCheckout> on mount — likely the same race condition (user is undefined, then code reads user.email / user.first_name in the proceed() closure / render). Add `if (!user || !pricing) return <Loader/>` GUARD before any user.* dereference, and only run the auth-redirect effect once `user === null`.

(Optional UX) The AI Editor Export tab currently shows the Export-now button even before any clip is uploaded. Either disable it pre-upload or render the Export tab only when stage === 'edit' so QA / users don't think it's a no-op.
critical_code_review_comments: PlanCheckout.jsx — `useEffect` treats `user === undefined` (still loading) the same as `user === null` (logged out). This is the root cause of the /plan-checkout failure. Pattern to use: `if (user === undefined) return; if (user === null) { navigate('/login?...'); return; }`.
PlanCheckout.jsx — `discounted` calc uses `Math.round(... * 100) / 100`. For 49 × 0.5 = 24.5 (fine). For yearly 468 × 0.5 = 234 (fine). Good.

PlanCheckout.jsx — `proceed()` references `user.first_name`, `user.last_name`, `user.display_name`, `user.email`. If `user` is somehow null when the button is clicked, this will throw. The loader guard above (lines 98-104) covers this in render, but proceed() should still null-check before destructuring.

Pricing.jsx CTA correctly switches text + destination based on user, but does NOT wait for auth-loading state — first paint will show 'Get Early Access →' even for logged-in users on a fresh tab. Minor UX flicker, acceptable.
ContentStudio.jsx deep-link useEffect correctly clears params via setSearchParams({}, {replace:true}) — verified refresh-safe.

rca_of_the_issue: PlanCheckout.jsx imports useAuth(), and inside its main useEffect it does `if (!user) navigate('/login?next=...')`. AuthProvider initializes user state to `undefined` and only resolves to the actual user object after /auth/me returns (one network round-trip). On mount, `!user` is true for `undefined`, so the redirect fires before the user object arrives. The login URL contains a nested encoded next param. After login (which itself honors next correctly), the user lands back on /plan-checkout, where the same race condition fires again. The user is stuck. Reproduction: log in as jane.doe.test → visit /pricing → click 'Upgrade to Creator →' → observe URL becomes /login?next=%2Flogin%3Fnext%3D%252Fplan-checkout… and the Sign in form re-appears. Mitigation: in PlanCheckout, treat `user === undefined` as 'still loading' (return a loader), only redirect when `user === null`. Same pattern should be audited across any other auth-gated pages.
